# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 2 THE HOUSE OF DREAMS

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Never in the entire history of Grey Shutters had the atmosphere held such intense excitement. Thirza herself was so thrilled that she was unable to hide it, an occurrence that bordered on the extraordinary.
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0000 }

“No wedding has ever taken place in this house,” she mentioned to Mrs. Agatha Sowerby, sounding somewhat apologetic. “During my childhood, an elderly clergyman remarked that a home fails to become a genuine one prior to being hallowed by a birth, a marriage, and a passing. Deaths have occurred in this place—both my mother and father passed away here, in addition to Obed; moreover, a birth has taken place here as well. A great while back, right after our relocation to this residence, a wedded farmhand worked for us briefly, and a infant was born to his wife here. Yet a marriage has never occurred previously. Thinking about Nell getting wedded feels incredibly odd. To an extent, she appears to me like nothing more than the young girl Obed carried home to this place fourteen years back. It is impossible for me to grasp her adulthood. My emotions upon witnessing Obed carrying in a GIRL will remain with me forever. I ponder the outcome of the boy who would have joined us had an error not transpired. I ponder the nature of HIS destiny.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0001 }

“Indeed, the error turned out to be lucky,” Mrs. Agatha Sowerby remarked, “even if, remember, I didn't hold that view initially—on the night I visited Nell and she made a huge fuss for us. A great deal has shifted since that moment, indeed.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0002 }

Mrs. Agatha let out a sigh, but she quickly became lively once more. If there were marriages to be arranged, Mrs. Agatha was willing to allow bygone days to be forgotten.
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0003 }

“Two of my cotton warp spreads are going to Nell,” she continued. “One with a tobacco stripe and another with an apple leaf. According to her, their popularity is actually returning. Regardless of what is fashionable, my opinion remains that a lovely apple-leaf spread is unmatched in beauty for a guest bed, and that is my final word. Bleaching them is something I need to attend to soon. Since the death of Thomas, I have kept them encased in cotton sacks, so their shade is surely terrible by now. Nevertheless, with a full month remaining, exposing them to dew will produce amazing results.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0004 }

Merely one month! Thirza let out a sigh, after which she remarked with pride:
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0005 }

“I am bestowing upon Nell the six braided rugs stored in my garret. It never occurred to me that she would desire them—they are terribly out of date, and modern preference seems entirely focused on hooked mats. Nevertheless, she requested them from me—stating that they were her absolute preference for her floors. Indeed, they ARE lovely. I crafted them using the finest rags, forming them into braided stripes. Creating them provided such companionship throughout these recent winters. Additionally, I intend to prepare a sufficient amount of blue plum preserve to supply her jam closet for a full year. It appears truly peculiar. Those blue plum trees failed to produce a single flower for three years, leading me to believe they should probably be chopped down. Yet this past spring they bloomed completely white, yielding a plum harvest larger than any I can recall at Grey Shutters.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0006 }

“Well, I am so grateful that Nell and Hugh are actually getting married in the end. I have constantly prayed for this,” Mrs. Agatha stated, speaking like someone who is pleasantly confident that her supplications accomplished a great deal. “Discovering that she actually had no intention of marrying the Portmaris man brought much peace of mind. Granted, he possessed wealth, whereas Hugh lacks money—at the outset, anyway; however, he is an Island boy.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0007 }

“He’s Hugh Carrow,” Thirza stated with satisfaction. Before expressing the idea that constantly lingered in the rear of her thoughts whenever she had observed Hugh since he was a child—the notion that he could have been HER son if not for her own stubborn pride a very long time ago—Thirza would have submitted to death itself. It seemed to Thirza that, through some odd mechanism, that past error would be corrected by his wedding to Nell. From the badness of the old resentment, something good had emerged.
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0008 }

Regarding Nell personally, her joy was so immense that it nearly terrified her. Ancient folklore claims that the gods dislike seeing humans who are exceedingly joyful. At the very least, it is true that particular people object to it. A pair of such individuals came down upon Nell one purple twilight and set about doing everything within their power to pop the iridescent sphere of her contentment. Should she believe she was securing any special catch in young Dr. Carrow, or should she fancy that his devotion to her remained as passionate as it perhaps was during his youth, they felt obligated to present the situation to her from a different viewpoint. Nevertheless, these two respectable women were not Nell's foes; rather, they were actually rather affectionate toward her, and they would have protected her like their own offspring if a third party had assailed her. Consistency is not required of human nature.
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0009 }

Mrs. Inglis—formerly Odette Pullen, as the Daily Enterprise described her—arrived alongside her mother and Mrs. Jasper Bell. However, time spent in marital arguments had failed to sour the gentle disposition within Odette. She had enjoyed a fortunate life. Although she had wed a wealthy man—a point Mrs. Agatha Sowerby would be sure to mention—her union had remained a joyful one. She remained uncorrupted by riches. She maintained the same tranquil, pleasant, rosy-faced nature that Odette had shown in the former group of four, sharing in the joy of her longtime friend and possessing a deep fascination with every delicate aspect of Nell’s trousseau, treating it with as much enthusiasm as if it were comparable to her own luxurious, gem-encrusted wardrobe. Cleverness was not Odette's strong suit, and she had likely never uttered a single notable thought throughout her existence; yet she refrained from speaking words that might injure the sentiments of others—a trait that, while passive, remains an uncommon and desirable quality.
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0010 }

“So Hugh did not betray your trust in the end,” Mrs. Gorham Pullen remarked, managing to infuse her voice with a hint of astonishment. “Indeed, the members of the Carrow family usually adhere to their promises after giving them, regardless of the circumstances. Let me think—you have reached twenty-five years of age, have you not, Nell? During my youth, turning twenty-five marked the initial milestone. Nevertheless, your appearance is remarkably youthful. Individuals with red hair invariably retain that look.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0011 }

“Very fashionable now is red hair,” Nell remarked, attempting a smile, though her tone was somewhat cool. Experience had fostered within her a humorous outlook that assisted her through numerous troubles; nevertheless, up to this point, no resource had succeeded in hardening her to any mention of her hair.
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0012 }

“Indeed it is—indeed it is,” Mrs. Gorham acknowledged. “No one can predict the odd whims that style will adopt. Now, Nell, your possessions are quite lovely, as well as being entirely appropriate for your social standing, wouldn't you say, Odette? My desire is that you find great joy. Be assured that you possess my finest hopes. An extended courtship rarely ends favorably. Nevertheless, given your circumstances, it was naturally unavoidable.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0013 }

“People may not put great trust in Hugh because he appears quite youthful for a physician,” Mrs. Jasper Bell remarked dejectedly. Following this, her lips pressed firmly together, signaling that she had fulfilled her obligation and absolved her mind. She fit the description of those individuals who perpetually wear a limp black plume in their headgear and have loose wisps of hair trailing down their necks.
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0014 }

The brief eclipse of Nell’s superficial joy in her lovely wedding attire quickly passed, leaving the profound depths of her underlying bliss untouched; furthermore, the minor gibes from Mesdames Bell and Pullen vanished from her mind upon Hugh’s arrival that evening, whereupon the couple strolled toward the brookside birches, which had grown from the young shoots present when Nell first arrived at Grey Shutters into majestic, pale pillars inside an enchanted realm of dusk and starlight. Sheltered by those dark shapes, Nell and Hugh conversed as sweethearts do regarding the residence they would share and the future that lay ahead for them both.
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0015 }

“I’ve discovered a home for us, Nell.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0016 }

“Ah, in what location? Surely not directly within the village, I trust. I would not entirely appreciate that.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0017 }

“No. In the village, a house could not be found. Halfway between Glen St. Agnes and Seven Gulls Point, on the harbor shore, stands this small white house. It is somewhat remote, though that will be less important once a ’phone is installed. Its location is lovely. Facing the sunset, it overlooks the vast blue harbor. Not far off are the sand-dunes, which the ocean winds sweep across and the sea spray soaks.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0018 }

“Yet what about the residence, Hugh,—the initial dwelling of OURS? How does it appear?”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0019 }

“It isn’t particularly big, yet it will be big enough for our needs. On the ground floor, you'll find a magnificent living room containing a fireplace, along with a dining room facing the harbor, plus a small room that can serve as my office. Its age is around sixty years—making it the most ancient house situated in Seven Gulls. However, it has been maintained in quite decent condition, having undergone a complete renovation approximately fifteen years back—it was shingled, plastered, and fitted with new flooring. From the start, the construction was sturdy. I gather that an element of romance was attached to how it was built, though the individual from whom I leased it was unaware of the details.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0020 }

“He stated that Captain Saul was the sole person able to tell that ancient tale at present.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0021 }

“What person is Captain Saul?”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0022 }

“The lighthouse tender at Seven Gulls Point. That Seven Gulls light will delight you, Nell. Its beam rotates, winking through the dusk similar to a grand star. From the windows of our living room and our front entrance, it is visible to us.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0023 }

“To whom does the house belong?”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0024 }

“Well, the Glen St. Agnes Presbyterian Church owns it currently, since I leased the place from its trustees. However, a very elderly woman, Miss Elizabeth Russell, was the owner until recently. Following her death this past spring, the Glen St. Agnes Church inherited her estate because no close kin survived her. The residence continues to hold her furnishings, a major portion of which I purchased—one could claim I got it for a mere song, as the trustees lost hope of finding a buyer due to its completely outdated style. I suspect the people of Glen St. Agnes have a preference for plush brocade along with sideboards that feature mirrors and decorative details. All the same, Miss Russell’s furnishings are of high quality, and I am certain it will appeal to you, Nell.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0025 }

“Up to this point, fine,” said Nell, giving a careful nod of agreement. “However, Hugh, individuals are unable to subsist on furniture by itself. You still have not brought up a single highly crucial detail. Do TREES exist around this house?”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0026 }

“A great deal of them, oh, dryad! Situated behind it is a large grove of fir trees, running down the lane are two rows of Lombardy poplars, and encircling a most charming garden is a ring of white birches. Right into the garden is where our front door opens, yet a second entrance exists—a small gate suspended between two firs. On one trunk are the hinges, while on the other is the catch. Overhead, an arch is created by their boughs.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0027 }

“Oh, I am deeply relieved! Residing in a place devoid of trees would be impossible for me—a crucial part of my spirit would perish from hunger. Indeed, following that admission, inquiring whether a stream exists nearby is pointless. Expecting THAT would be overstepping.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0028 }

“However, a brook DOES exist—and it truly flows through a single corner of the garden.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0029 }

“Then,” Nell remarked, letting out an extended sigh of complete contentment, “the residence you located IS the exact house of my dreams.”
{: #nw-v04-c02-p0030 }
